events.title: First Meeting
events.context: The Constituent Assembly meets for the first time to begin creating India's Constitution. A leader is needed for this historic meeting.
events.question: Who should lead the first meeting?

options.text: Jawaharlal Nehru - Popular freedom fighter
options.feedback: Not quite. While Nehru was very popular, he wasn't chosen for the first meeting.

options.text: Sachchidananda Sinha - Oldest and most experienced
options.feedback: Correct! Sinha was chosen as temporary chairman for being the eldest member.

options.text: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar - Legal expert
options.feedback: Not correct. While Ambedkar had great legal expertise, he wasn't chosen to lead the first meeting.

events.title: Objectives Resolution
events.context: Nehru presents the Objectives Resolution outlining the values that should guide India's Constitution: Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.
events.question: Why did these four values matter for India's Constitution?

options.text: They address India's specific challenges
options.feedback: Correct! Each value addressed a different challenge India faced. These became the Constitution's Preamble.

options.text: They sound impressive and democratic
options.feedback: Not correct. Values weren't chosen just because they sound impressive.

options.text: Other countries also had these values
options.feedback: Not quite. India didn't choose them simply because other countries had them.

events.title: Drafting Committee
events.context: India is free. A Drafting Committee is formed to write the Constitution.
events.question: Who should be chosen as chairman of the Drafting Committee?

options.text: Jawaharlal Nehru - Popular freedom fighter
options.feedback: Not correct. While Nehru was popular, drafting needed legal expertise.

options.text: Sardar Patel - Experienced administrator
options.feedback: Not quite. Patel was a great administrator but drafting required legal expertise.

options.text: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar - Expert in law and equality
options.feedback: Correct! Ambedkar's legal expertise and commitment to equality made him the perfect choice.

events.title: Parliamentary System
events.context: The Assembly debates whether India should follow a Parliamentary system or Presidential system.
events.question: Why should India choose Parliamentray system?

options.text: Britain had this system, so we followed it
options.feedback: Not correct. India didn't choose it just because Britain had it.

options.text: The government stays accountable to Parliament daily
options.feedback: Correct! Parliament can question ministers and remove the government.

options.text: It makes the government more stable
options.feedback: Not quite. Parliamentary systems are less stable but more accountable.

events.title: Language Policy
events.context: India has many languages. The Assembly must decide the official language policy.
events.question: What language provision should go into the Constitution?

options.text: Only Hindi - One national language
options.feedback: Not correct. This would exclude non-Hindi speakers.

options.text: Each state chooses its own language
options.feedback: Not quite. The Union government needed common languages.

options.text: Hindi and English both as official languages
options.feedback: Correct! This balanced identity with diversity.

events.title: Property Rights
events.context: The Assembly debates whether property should be a fundamental right.
events.question: What should the Constitution say about property rights?

options.text: Balance both - Right to property with rules for public good
options.feedback: Correct! Property was protected but could be acquired for public use with compensation.

options.text: Property is absolute - No one can take it
options.feedback: Not correct. This would block public projects.

options.text: No private property - Everything belongs to state
options.feedback: Not quite. This would remove individual freedom.

events.title: Constitution Ready
events.context: After three years of debates, the Constitution is adopted.
events.question: What makes India's Constitution special?

options.text: It is very long and detailed
options.feedback: Not quite. Length shows thoroughness but not uniqueness.

options.text: It balances unity with diversity
options.feedback: Correct! Strong centre with state freedom keeps India united.

options.text: It copied from many countries
options.feedback: Not correct. It adapted ideas to suit India.

events.title: India Becomes Republic
events.context: January 26, 1950 arrives — a historic day for India.
events.question: Why is January 26, 1950 important?

options.text: India got independence from British
options.feedback: Not correct. Independence was on August 15, 1947.

options.text: First elections were held
options.feedback: Not quite. First elections were in 1951–52.

options.text: The Constitution came into effect
options.feedback: Correct! India became a Republic on this day.
